correctness.rationale: A positive Parseval rule is precisely a probability measure annihilating nonzero differences A-A. At p prime every square Fourier minor is nonsingular (Chebotarev), forcing at least |A-A| nodes; Caratheodory compresses the complete uniform measure to at most that many. The same nonsingularity gives unique weights and a simplex-origin positivity test. Cauchy-Davenport and its Vosper equality case classify fixed-cardinality minima, while cyclotomic irreducibility forces all p nodes for equal weights. The composite-six counterexample shows prime necessity; singleton and p=2 are handled explicitly.
